title: Jurassic Park
synopsis: Isla Nublar. A theme park, soft-opening. The fences are electric and the dinosaurs are alive. The power, in two hours, will go off.

nodes.text: You and Ellie arrive. Hammond grins. A brachiosaurus stands beyond the trees. The Lab is already waiting. What changes is whether “Marvel” or “Ask how” is the instinct you carry into it. By The Lab, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You marvel. The path to The Lab opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to ask how. It carries you toward The Lab, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Vials, amber, frogs filling gaps in DNA. Tour Cars comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Object on principle” and “Reserve judgement.” By Tour Cars, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You commit to object on principle. It carries you toward Tour Cars, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to reserve judgement. It carries you toward Tour Cars, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Self-driving Jeeps. Lex and Tim in the back. You cannot avoid Rain; you can only decide whether “Make conversation” or “Watch the road” defines the person who reaches it. By Rain, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You choose to make conversation. By Rain, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You watch the road. The path to Rain opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The sky opens. A goat is offered. The T. rex does not appear. Both choices lead to Power Off, but “Wait” arrives there with a different cost than “Volunteer to look.” In Rain, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to wait. By Power Off, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to volunteer to look. By Power Off, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The fences go dark. The T. rex notices. The car splits in half. Tree comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Run” and “Stand still.” By Tree, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You commit to run. It carries you toward Tree, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You stand still. The path to Tree opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Up a tree, with Tim, with the broken car above you. You cannot avoid Ellie and Muldoon; you can only decide whether “Climb down” or “Stay up” defines the person who reaches it. At Ellie and Muldoon, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You climb down. The path to Ellie and Muldoon opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to stay up. It carries you toward Ellie and Muldoon, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Search and rescue. Muldoon has a gun. Ellie has a flashlight. The road still runs toward Sick Triceratops. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Help them search” and choosing “Find the kids.”

choices.consequence: You choose to help them search. By Sick Triceratops, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to find the kids. It carries you toward Sick Triceratops, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Ellie crouches by it, hand on the hide. Visitor Center is already waiting. What changes is whether “Help her diagnose” or “Watch the trees” is the instinct you carry into it. By Visitor Center, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You choose to help her diagnose. By Visitor Center, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to watch the trees. By Visitor Center, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Ice cream melts on the table. Hammond, smaller. You cannot avoid Kitchen; you can only decide whether “Comfort him briefly” or “Find the kids” defines the person who reaches it. In Visitor Center, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You comfort him briefly. The path to Kitchen opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to find the kids. It carries you toward Kitchen, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Velociraptors. Lex hides in cabinets. Tim freezes. Hammond's Confession will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Distract them” than after “Trap them in the freezer.” In Kitchen, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You commit to distract them. It carries you toward Hammond's Confession, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You trap them in the freezer. The path to Hammond's Confession opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: He says he should have been there for them. He sounds, briefly, like a grandfather and not a CEO. Power Restoration will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Forgive him later” than after “Hold the line now.”

choices.consequence: You commit to forgive him later. It carries you toward Power Restoration, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to hold the line now. It carries you toward Power Restoration, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Lex types on the Unix system. The lights come on. You cannot avoid Raptors Outside; you can only decide whether “Praise her” or “Stay alert” defines the person who reaches it. In Power Restoration, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You praise her. The path to Raptors Outside opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to stay alert. It carries you toward Raptors Outside, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: They are at the door. The door is glass. The road still runs toward Climb the Bones. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Move the kids up” and choosing “Distract the raptors.”

choices.consequence: You move the kids up. The path to Climb the Bones opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You distract the raptors. The path to Climb the Bones opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The big skeleton in the rotunda. You climb. The raptors follow. You cannot avoid T. Rex Returns; you can only decide whether “Climb fast” or “Climb carefully” defines the person who reaches it. In Climb the Bones, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You climb fast. The path to T. Rex Returns opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You climb carefully. The path to T. Rex Returns opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The T. rex bursts in, takes one raptor, then another. The banner falls. For one suspended beat, T. Both choices lead to Helicopter Pad, but “Run for the helicopter” arrives there with a different cost than “Stay till the dust settles.”

choices.consequence: You run for the helicopter. The path to Helicopter Pad opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You stay till the dust settles. The path to Helicopter Pad opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Hammond, mute. Ellie. The kids in your arms. Hammond is already waiting. What changes is whether “Hold them” or “Look at the island a last time” is the instinct you carry into it. At Hammond, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You hold them. The path to Hammond opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Look at the island a last time
choices.consequence: You commit to look at the island a last time. It carries you toward Hammond, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: He, finally, agrees not to endorse the park. He looks small. He looks human. Flight Out comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Be kind” and “Be honest.” In Hammond, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to be kind. By Flight Out, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to be honest. By Flight Out, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The birds, you realize, are dinosaurs. The window is full of pelicans. The road still runs toward Mainland. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Notice it” and choosing “Sleep.” In Flight Out, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You commit to notice it. It carries you toward Mainland, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to sleep. It carries you toward Mainland, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Press, cameras, no statement. Both choices lead to The Lab Visit, but “No statement” arrives there with a different cost than “A short statement.” At The Lab Visit, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to no statement. It carries you toward The Lab Visit, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You choose to a short statement. By The Lab Visit, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Years later you visit a different lab. The science is, again, ahead of the ethics. You decide what to do. Coffee with Ellie is already waiting. What changes is whether “Speak publicly” or “Step away” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You speak publicly. The path to Coffee with Ellie opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You choose to step away. By Coffee with Ellie, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Years on, coffee with Ellie. You both still wake at 4 a.m. sometimes. “Plan an article” draws you toward The Paper; “Just enjoy the coffee” leaves Back to the Field waiting on the other side. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps The Kids Grew Up in play.

choices.consequence: You commit to plan an article. It carries you toward The Paper, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to just enjoy the coffee. It carries you toward Back to the Field, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You commit to take the third path. It carries you toward The Kids Grew Up, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You and Ellie publish a long paper on de-extinction ethics. It becomes the standard syllabus. You don't, you decide, need to be the regulator. You just need to be the alarm. The road into The Paper began with “Plan an article” in Coffee with Ellie; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You return to paleontology. You discover, in a Montana dig, a fossil that, briefly, shakes the field. You realize the living dinosaurs were, for you, a detour. The road into Back to the Field began with “Just enjoy the coffee” in Coffee with Ellie; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Lex becomes a programmer. Tim becomes a paleontologist. They both, separately, send you Christmas cards. The cards are, always, slightly nicer than yours. The road into The Kids Grew Up began with “Take the third path” in Coffee with Ellie; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
